# Poikiloderma Congenitale

**Authors:** Wissem Hafsi, Talel Badri

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Congenital poikiloderma, also known as Rothmund-Thomson syndrome (RTS), is a rare genodermatosis of autosomal recessive (AR) inheritance characterized by a typical erythema facial (poikiloderma) of early-onset, associated with different clinical features including short stature, sparse scalp hair, absent or sparse eyelashes or eyebrows, juvenile cataracts, skeletal abnormalities, juvenile cataract, premature aging, and susceptibility to osteosarcoma. See Image. Poikiloderma Congenitale. There are 2 types of RTS. Type 1 is characterized by rapidly progressive, bilateral, juvenile cataracts. In contrast, congenital bone abnormalities and an increased risk of osteosarcoma in childhood and squamous cell carcinoma at an older age characterize type 2.
